answer: Arrival-timing skew scoring. Each new identity gains standing only from its first outbound actions arriving across a spread of wake windows, so bursts near dawn count less than a gradual trickle. The system scores a vertex by how evenly its early traffic fills those windows, and identity clusters that share timing collapse into one score. An attacker must run each fake identity on its own staggered schedule for days, paying real compute and rent, which is the crystal cost of scale.
